text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.

-The European Commission approved a proposed salmon deal between the European Union and Norway late last night. A minimum price on salmon import will be implemented, but Norway avoids anti-dumping taxes.

-Jon Gundersen, head of the Storebrand board, says he believes Norwegian conglomerate Orkla will end up supporting the proposed merger between Norway's largest insurer Storebrand and the country's second largest commercial bank Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse. Orkla holds 9.9 percent of the shares in Storebrand.
-Heinrich Schembecker, manager at Germany's Commerzbank, says the Norwegian crown will be strengthened when the euro is introduced. He also believes interest rates will be lower.
-Fast-food chain McDonalds stopped selling salmon burgers in Norway last night after four people fell sick and were taking to hospital after eating salmon burgers in Oslo.
-Computer trouble caused by the switch to the year 2000 will cost Norwegian industry and the Norwegian state a total of 30 billion crowns. Many software programmes will stop or malfunction.
-Norwegian port authorities have signed a deal with three large shipowners for the reduction of sulphur emissions.
